name: Galvia

attributes.attribute: gave her name to the county of Galway
was a princess who drowned in the river that bears her name
was likely once a goddess of the watershed like Sínann and Bóand

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Galvia was an Irish mythological figure. She was obscure. The county of Galway takes its name from her. She was said to be a princess. She drowned in the river that bears her name. The same tale is told of the goddesses Sínann and Bóand. Galvia was likely once an important goddess of the watershed.

okr.objective: Record the Irish figure Galvia and her link to the county of Galway.
key_results: Trace the county name Galway to the figure Galvia.
Describe the character of the woman who drowned in her own river.
